text:
tayla: hey all, first-day snag. VPN (WireGuard newhire-prod) is connected on Windows but inside WSL2 Ubuntu I can't curl or docker pull from our internal registry (internal.registry.redwood.internal). From Windows PowerShell `curl https://intranet.redwood.internal` works, but inside WSL `curl https://intranet.redwood.internal` times out. Anyone seen WSL2 networking weirdness with split-tunnel VPNs? :confused:

it-ops: welcome! WSL2 has its own virtualized network namespace behind the Host NAT (vEthernet (WSL)). Often the host gets VPN routes but the WSL VM keeps using the host NAT nameserver (172.25.x.x) and doesn't inherit host routes/DNS. Quick checks: inside WSL, what's `cat /etc/resolv.conf` and `ip route`?

tayla: inside WSL `cat /etc/resolv.conf` shows `nameserver 172.22.176.1` and `ip route` shows default via 172.22.176.1 dev eth0. On Windows `ipconfig` shows wg0 with 10.10.2.x and DNS 10.10.0.53. So looks like WSL isn't using the VPN DNS and maybe not routing to the VPN.

wsl-expert: yep that's the usual. Two approaches that have worked for folks:
1) Make WSL use the internal DNS and routes from the host: set a static resolv.conf inside WSL and disable auto-gen. Steps:```# in WSL
sudo rm /etc/resolv.conf
echo "nameserver 10.10.0.53" | sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf
# prevent WSL from overwriting resolv.conf
sudo bash -c 'cat > /etc/wsl.conf <<\'EOF
[network]
generateResolvConf = false
EOF'
# then from Windows PowerShell restart WSL
wsl --shutdown
# start WSL again and test
```
This forces the distro to query the internal DNS so name resolution for internal.hosts works.

2) If the issue is routing (DNS resolves but TCP times out), WSL's NAT may not forward traffic to the host VPN. A workaround is to forward specific ports via the Windows host or add route rules on the Windows side to NAT traffic from the WSL subnet to the VPN. For example, on Windows (admin PowerShell) you can add a route for the internal subnet pointing to the wg0 gateway for the WSL subnet:```# find your WSL virtual adaptor subnet via `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu ip route` and find the gateway on Windows, then:
New-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix 10.10.0.0/16 -InterfaceAlias "vEthernet (WSL)" -NextHop 10.10.2.1 -RouteMetric 1```
This approach is fiddly and requires admin rights; prefer option 1 unless you need transparent routing for many services.

tayla: tried option 1. I set generateResolvConf=false and wrote /etc/resolv.conf to 10.10.0.53, then `wsl --shutdown`. After restarting WSL, `dig @10.10.0.53 intranet.redwood.internal +short` returns the internal IP but `curl` still timed out.

wsl-expert: ok so DNS isn't the blocker. That suggests the WSL NAT path isn't sending packets into the VPN tunnel. Quick test from Windows: can you `ping` the internal IP (e.g., `ping 10.10.3.5`) and then from WSL `ping 10.10.3.5` and compare? Also check Windows firewall—some rules block forwarded traffic from WSL to the VPN.

it-ops: also check the WireGuard client settings on Windows. If the client is configured to only bind to the host adapter and not allow LAN/local subnet access, the host might not NAT WSL traffic into the tunnel. In our managed profile we enable "AllowLAN"/"Allow local network" equivalents. If you used a consumer client or custom profile, that could explain it.

tayla: ping from Windows to 10.10.3.5 succeeds. From WSL ping to 10.10.3.5 shows packets leaving but no replies (100% loss). Windows Defender firewall was on; I temporarily disabled it and WSL `curl` worked. So definitely firewall/NAT issue.

jamie: great diagnostic. Two practical fixes we push in onboarding docs: a) for managed machines we add a firewall rule that allows the WSL virtual switch to use the VPN interface (Windows Defender inbound/outbound rules allowing vEthernet (WSL) -> wg0 for internal subnets). b) if you can't change firewall (personal device), run Docker and other clients on the Windows host or use Docker Desktop's WSL2 integration but ensure Docker daemon is running in WSL and uses the host DNS; sometimes toggling Docker Desktop integration to the distro helps.

it-ops: action items: we'll add a small script for Windows admins to create the necessary firewall/NAT rules:```# PowerShell (admin)
# allow WSL vEthernet to connect to internal subnet via wg0
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "WSL to Internal VPN" -Direction Outbound -InterfaceAlias "vEthernet (WSL)" -RemoteAddress 10.10.0.0/16 -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "WSL to Internal VPN Inbound" -Direction Inbound -InterfaceAlias "vEthernet (WSL)" -LocalAddress 10.10.0.0/16 -Action Allow
```
We'll pair on exact InterfaceAlias names per image.

tayla: applied the temporary firewall allow and WSL `docker pull internal.registry.redwood.internal:5000/my-app:latest` succeeded. :tada: Thanks!

wsl-expert: adding a small WSL-specific note to the onboarding VPN doc: 1) If using WSL2, set generateResolvConf=false and pin /etc/resolv.conf to 10.10.0.53 to fix DNS, 2) ensure host firewall/NAT allows vEthernet (WSL) traffic to the VPN, or use Docker Desktop WSL integration with daemon in WSL. We'll include PowerShell one-liners and the wsl --shutdown step.

devex-bot: created ticket #INFR-4333 to add WSL2 (Windows) troubleshooting: resolv.conf pinning, firewall/NAT rules, and Docker Desktop notes to the new-hire checklist and onboarding docs.

tayla: leaving this here for other new-hires: WSL2 can be a gotcha on day one if internal services resolve but won't connect, check resolv.conf and Windows firewall/NAT for the WSL vEthernet interface. Saved my first-hour debugging. :relieved:
